notes.title: Ranked Integrity Update – Rookie Rank Exploit

items.text: We recently identified and quickly resolved an exploit that allowed some players, primarily on PlayStation 5, to enter Ranked matches as Rookie IV regardless of their actual rank.

notes.title: This caused several unintended advantages, including

items.text: No Ranked entry cost
Rookie-tier kill bonuses
Matchmaking Rating (MMR) being recorded as 0
RP earned during these matches still being added to the player's actual Ranked score
This created an unfair advantage and directly impacted the integrity of Ranked progression.

Our Anti-Cheat team identified the root cause and deployed a fix to prevent further abuse. We also conducted an investigation into accounts that benefited from this exploit and took enforcement action against players who deliberately and egregiously abused it.
A total of 906 accounts have been banned, with suspension lengths determined by the amount of RP gained through exploitation:
731 accounts were banned for 120 days for illegitimately amassing approximately 4,999 RP
107 accounts were banned for 240 days for illegitimately amassing 5,000–9,999 RP
67 accounts were banned for 365 days for illegitimately amassing 10,000+ RP
PC: 12
PlayStation: 848
Xbox: 44
Nintendo Switch 2: 2
Total RP deducted: 15,112,554

We recognize that some players may have encountered this issue unintentionally. Through our investigation, we were able to precisely identify cases of unintended interaction and distinguish them from deliberate abuse. Those accounts were not actioned.

Ranked integrity depends on a fair and consistent competitive environment. Exploits that undermine matchmaking, bypass Ranked entry requirements, or provide illegitimate progression will be investigated and actioned.
Our team will continue monitoring Ranked, looking for similar activity and addressing vulnerabilities that could be used to compromise competitive integrity.
CIPHER OVERVIEW

[p align="start"]Apex Legends: Cipher is here! It’s bringing new features, new weapon combos, and big changes to Ranked alongside the usual slew of bug fixes and balancing passes. Read on for info about the Akimbo Wingman, Strongholds, new Ranked features and more! Season 31 begins on November 3rd, so get the squad together and get ready to jump into Apex Legends: Cipher!

notes.title: RANKED LEGEND BANNING AND SCORING ADJUSTMENTS

items.text: [p align="start"]We recently unveiled upcoming plans for new features, quality of life improvements, and adjustments coming to Ranked over the next two seasons.

[p align="start"]Starting in Cipher, we’re launching Legend Banning in Diamond+ matches, allowing you to vote for Legends to be banned from selection for each match. Scoring adjustments for wide-skill matches will also be live at season start and will adjust entry costs if your Rank is too far above or below the median lobby rank.
[p align="start"]Read on for all of the details, or circle back to the Ranked Roadmap blog to see what’s still on the horizon.

[p align="start"]E-District Night Adjustments
Balanced Silhouette Contrast: Reduced the extreme difference between direct and ambient light levels, lifting deep shadows to dramatically improve enemy player visibility in low-light zones
Motivated Light Sources: Added a significant number of localized, practical light fixtures to ensure the map feels naturally illuminated by the environment itself
Grounding & Shadows: Substantially increased the technical budget for shadow-casting lights, grounding characters and environment structures far more realistically
Micro-Contrast & Mood: Reworked the color-correction pass to sharpen micro-contrast, maintaining the city's rich cyberpunk atmosphere without turning dark areas into blind spots
Visual Noise Reduction: Streamlined building and advertisement panel colouration to clear up high-frequency visual noise, letting player silhouettes pop against the city backdrop
[p align="start"]Global Rendering & Readability Updates
[p align="start"]These engine-wide updates apply to all maps following our latest rendering upgrades:
Environmental Illumination: Applied a comprehensive lighting and material pass to world geometry and signage, establishing unified visual standards across all maps
Luminance Standardization: Standardized world lighting values to guarantee predictable character contrast and consistent material behavior across different environments
Atmospheric Fog Overhaul: Re-architected our fog systems within active gameplay spaces to preserve critical sightlines while sharpening overall depth perception
Auto-Exposure Adaptation: Fine-tuned global color grading and slowed down auto-exposure adaptation speeds, limiting drastic brightness shifts and reducing eye strain during high-intensity fights
Performance Optimization: Rebalanced localized lighting grids to optimize GPU performance and improve target readability in high-frequency visual areas

[p align="start"]This season introduces a new system that allows players to select Legends they would like to see banned at the start of each Diamond+ match.
[p align="start"]The Legend banning system is designed to help disrupt dominant Legend meta match-over-match.

[p align="start"]In the new match starting flow, each player may request one Legend to ban. When the request timer ends, all requests are collected and tallied. A Legend's chance of being banned equals its share of all requests. For example, if Wraith receives 80% of the lobby's requests, Wraith has an 80% chance of being banned on the first randomized selection. Currently, the system selects 2 Legends to ban.

[p align="start"]If fewer than 4 unique Legends are requested, the system picks from the previous week's most played Legends and adds 1 request to each, bringing the total unique Legends that have a possibility to be banned to the minimum of 4.
[p align="start"]Once all banned Legends have been chosen, all players will proceed to Legend selection, with the currently banned Legends unavailable for selection.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: We are continuing to experiment with ways to improve the matchmaking experience, and in the meantime we want to account for frustrating and unfair matches in the scoring system. We landed on this system of decreasing entry cost for disadvantaged teams AND increasing it for advantaged teams as it best reflects the differences in RP earned while also avoiding making the RP system inflationary.

[p align="start"]We are adding new Ranked Match Types to account for times when your squad is unfairly matched. These should be uncommon, usually occurring when playing outside of peak hours, but when they occur your entry cost will be fairly adjusted.
Challenger Match - discounts entry cost by 30% when your Squad Tier is 2+ tiers below the Lobby Tier.
Goliath Match - increases entry cost by 50% when your Squad Tier is 2+ tiers above the Lobby Tier.
[p align="start"]If you are in a Goliath or Challenger Match, you will be told on the Waiting for Players screen and when you exit the dropship.

[p align="start"]Your Squad Tier is calculated from the average RP of each squadmate, though all premade squadmates’ RPs are treated as equal to the value of the highest squadmate’s RP within their premade group.

For example, if you are in a two person premade and you have the highest RP at 5,000 RP, your premade teammate's RP will also be treated as 5,000 RP. A player who is not a part of your premade will have no RP adjustment.
If a teammate never connects, your Squad Tier is decreased by one full tier.
[p align="start"]The match’s Lobby Tier is the median of all Squad Tiers.

📋TESTING: We have activated a matchmaking test that increases maximum queue times for Plat+ players on all platforms, in all regions. The queue time increase scales with Rank tier, and Masters players could expect a maximum extension of approximately 30 seconds.

This test is in pursuit of tighter skill bands in high skill matches and less spill over of high rank players into mid-rank matches, as the matchmaker spends more time prioritizing the tightest possible lobbies before expanding its search. This test will run until the end of the season, or until we have enough data.
Please continue to give feedback on if you are experiencing tighter matchmaking.

Following early data showing promising impacts to queue times and tighter match skill-widths, we will be expanding this test to Wildcard matchmaking as well. This text expansion will be live at 10am PT, on October 16th and will impact players on all platforms in US-West.

Starting tomorrow, October 7th at approximately 10am PT, we will be conducting a matchmaking test by enabling cross-play as the default option for all players, on all platforms in the US-West servers. The intention of this test is to shorten queue times and tighten matchmaking skill bands. This test will run until the season ends on November 3rd. Console players can opt out of the test by turning off cross-play in your settings menu.

We are continuing to track community feedback regarding Apex KO and are making a few additional tuning changes to address player painpoints.

releases.displayName: Apex Legends™: Marked Midseason Patch Notes

items.text: [p align="start"]Welcome back to Split 2 of Apex Legends: Marked. To start the second half of the season, we’ve got Legend balancing changes, some adjustment to loot availability (including more healing items), buffs to a trio of long range weapons, and the usual array of tweaks, fixes and adjustments. Split 2 starts on September 15th, so assemble your squad and get ready to jump back into Marked!

[p align="start"]In the leadup to Split 2, we implemented significant, new systems to detect players using unauthorized controller hardware or software in Apex Legends on all platforms including: PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch 2.

[p align="start"]Prior to implementation, we spent several months thoroughly validating these systems to ensure they can accurately identify prohibited behavior. Players that trigger these detections will be actioned upon and may be banned accordingly upon review. Playing on console does not make you exempt from detection or enforcement.
[p align="start"]This is just the beginning for these new systems which we will continue to improve to keep pace with evolving cheating methods.

[p align="start"]We want the community to know that we are actively working to identify and remove cheaters at every level of play — including the highest ranks. Thank you to everyone who reports suspicious behavior and helps us keep Apex Legends fair.
[p align="start"]For more anti-cheat information, check out our most recent update!

[p align="start"]Dev note: Our main goal is to give Conduit players more avenues for skill expression and to ensure her abilities feel functional, readable, and fluid. Apex’s Shield Healer saw a big uptick in her success throughout Season 29 thanks to some overhauls to her Tactical and its associated upgrades. Despite Conduit receiving a few nerfs since then, we still wanted to come back to her this Season to focus on polishing and refining her Ultimate, as mentioned in the Season 29 Designer’s Notes. Beyond her base kit, we wanted to give Conduit two brand new Level 2 Upgrades that are now fully unique to her and emphasize different aspects of her aggressive support style.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Added preview visuals on the shield bar to indicate how much Temp Shield will be generated by the end of the regen period.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Various aspects of the Ultimate’s deployment have been smoothed out, meaning it fires faster and gets you back to guns sooner.
Can now toggle orientation while targeting to deploy jammers in a forward line.
Added a new HUD element to better inform players if their deployment location will cause jammers to break.
Also, individual jammer indicators now turn red if they would break at the current targeting location.
Jammers now spawn higher and slightly closer together, creating a tighter formation that covers more vertical space.
Jammers activate significantly faster, establishing the barricade’s threat area quicker.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Both Level 2 Upgrades, Battpack and Bigger Jam, have been removed.
NEW: Concurrency (Level 2)
Refire Energy Barricade once with no cooldown within 10s of initial firing.
Jammers spawn in a tighter formation with 2 less jammers.
NEW: Jammed Up (Level 2)
[p align="start"]Energy Barricade’s jammers have a 25% larger radius and enemies damaged by them have their HUD jammed for 10s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Though this grenadier has seen a gradual increase in play over time since his rework in Season 28, we wanted to revisit him to address the community feedback that we didn’t hit the efficacy, impact, and responsiveness expected of a new Motherlode. We’re also making some big shakeups to his Upgrade configuration that impact the rest of his kit, including incorporating Wreckless and Knuckle Cluster into his base kit (with some nerfs). Rest assured, we’ll be keeping a close eye on him, as our intention is to add more hype tech to Fuse’s toolbox without pushing him toward being a Legend defined by his movement. He will always be Apex’s explosives expert first and foremost!
[p align="start"]Passive
Added 25% Explosive Damage Resistance at base and can see ordinances highlighted in the world within 30m of him.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Fuse can now Knuckle Jump at base.
Jumping no longer provides Tactical cooldown reduction.
Jump power moderately decreased, so Fuse will gain less momentum when jumping.
Now displays a visual indicator that signifies the radius where the jump can be activated.
Significantly decreased the time it takes to return to guns after firing.
Players can now ADS while aiming to zoom.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Slightly decreased the raise time.
Adjusted the firing arc with the focus on the main explosive projectile landing more quickly and responsively.
Added an indicator to visualize the radius of the initial and subsequent explosions.
Decreased the time it takes for the mini-bombs to explode, speeding up the rollout of explosions.
Decreased the damage falloff on the initial explosion, meaning enemies closer to the edge of the radius will take a higher percentage of the maximum damage.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Knuckle Jumper (Level 2) and Wreckless (Level 3) have been removed.
Reignition has been moved from Level 3 to Level 2.
Pyro Techniques (Level 2)
Doubled the radius of the persistent flames.
Reignition (Level 2)
Decreased Ultimate Recharge Rate from 1s per 2 explosive damage to 1s per 3 explosive damage.
NEW: Big Bang (Level 3)
Knuckle Cluster’s explosions cover a 50% larger area.
NEW: Sticky Bomb (Level 3)
Knuckle Cluster’s initial projectile is 25% larger and sticks to enemies. Every 7 hits on an enemy reduces Knuckle Cluster’s cooldown by 1s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Catalyst saw a small boost in pick rate after her buffs in Season 28, but we felt she needed more love using a slightly different approach since her stats didn’t hold. This Season, we’re focusing more holistically on smoothing out the tension of moving from base to base amongst the fast pace of action. We want Cat’s building experience to be fun and flexible, so giving her more options to customize her space and adding in some longtime community-requested quality-of-life features will empower players to feel rewarded for putting in the work to master her. We’re also making big swings on shuffling up her upgrades, including a new Level 3 upgrade, Ferro-Frenzy, that will really shake up how we see players approach their setup.
[p align="start"]Passive
Catalyst is no longer immune to other Catalysts’ abilities.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Now automatically reinforces or rebuilds doors if colliding with a valid door or doorway on placement.
Decreased Cooldown from 20s to 15s.
Increased Spike Height, meaning that players can less easily jump over them.
Hitting enemies with the projectile will now deal damage to them.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Significantly decreased firing time, making it smoother to deploy and raise the wall.
Allies are no longer slowed or blinded when passing through the wall.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Sole Piercer (Level 2) has been removed.
Hidden Spikes has been moved from Level 2 to Level 3.
Resilient Veil and Ferro-Door have been moved from Level 3 to Level 2.
Ferro-Door (Level 2)
Now also increases max reinforced doors from 4 to 6.
Resilient Veil (Level 2)
Now also decreases Ultimate Cooldown from 150s to 120s.
NEW: Ferro-Frenzy (Level 3)
Your max Spike count is increased by 1. Spikes are 50% smaller, but deal faster tick damage.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Bloodhound got some significant changes for this season but they haven’t been as impactful on their pick and encounter win rates as we hoped. With these updates we’re hoping to add some improvements to their Ultimate and Tactical. We’ll continue to monitor Bloodhound’s performance and adjust if needed.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Reduced cloak visibility while in dome.
Ring damage no longer drops cloak.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Added 1 extra second on scan length.
Tweaked to provide more frequent snapshots, but the snapshots fade over time.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Sonar snapshots begin fading more quickly.
Sonar snapshots should disappear more readily when seeing the head of either the snapshot or the player being tracked.
[p align="start"]Back to Top

[p align="start"]Dev note: For an ability with a short cooldown that can have a devastating effect on one target, the Kickstart drone needs more counterplay options. Even when the victim decides to destroy the drone, the high health pool often makes that hard to do, especially in close quarters when Axle is quickly following up, herself. For cases when destroying it isn’t an option, at least the victim should be able to have more agency about where they get displaced with the knockback nerf and decreased stun.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Nitro Gate launch speed reduced from 750 to 700.
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Ultimate HP reduced from 200 to 150.
Base Ultimate cooldown increased from 90s to 120s.
Ultimate knockback arc widened and max height reduced.
Ultimate stun duration reduced from 1.5s to 0.25s.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Jump Gate replaced with a new Drone Deployer Upgrade that brings the Ult cooldown back down to 90s.

[p align="start"]Dev note: The turn slow punishment on the Seer tactical was very frustrating to fight against. We’ve decided to remove the turn slow since the tactical output is still strong without it.
Removed turn slow when hit by the Tactical
[p align="start"]Back to Top

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Last season, we made a huge change to loot distribution and spawning (read our retrospective in this update’s designer’s notes!). After reviewing the data and feedback from the community, we are making some minor adjustments to healing, ammo, and weapon availability. Healing was becoming scarcer than intended, and due to the removal of energy ammo, the other ammo types were spawning ammo boxes at higher rates than intended.

[p align="start"]Bin Resets have been adjusted to be closer to its pre-Season 30 version but keeps the original intent of reducing its overall spike to player power. The Season 30 version was not providing the density of necessities needed to quickly re-stock for the end game. Reset Bins now have more items on average with healing, ammo, survival slot items, and amps spawning more frequently inside.

[p align="start"]The Weapon Assist feature previously only included a small selection of pistols, shotguns and the Alternator. To help players find higher quality weapons off the drop, we are expanding this to now include all available weapons.

[p align="start"]These adjustments help to address some of the pain points we have been seeing while maintaining the overall goal of last update’s changes of creating an overall healthier loot curve as the game progresses.
[p align="start"]We will continue to monitor your feedback and make adjustments as quickly as we can!
[p align="start"]Loot Pool Spawn Rates (Pre-Bin Reset)
Increased availability of healing items.
Slightly decreased availability of ammo.
[p align="start"]Loot Bin Reset
Increased average count of items spawned per bin
Healing
Ammo
Survival Slot items
Amps
[p align="start"]Loot Bin Logic
Updated loot bin logic to significantly reduce the possibility of empty loot bins spawning in game.
The weapon pool for Weapon Assist (opening your first loot bin of the match while having no weapons in your inventory) now has the chance to spawn all base weapons.
Previously could only spawn a selection of pistols, shotguns, and the Alternator.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Season 30 was a large shakeup to the weapon meta and we want to let things settle a bit more before making any big changes. We are buffing a few weapons that were previously falling behind and have continued to fall after Season 30.
[p align="start"]Triple Take
Increased rate of fire while in ADS.
Blue magazine increased from 8 to 9.
[p align="start"]Bocek Compound Bow
Increased arrow stockpile from 40 to 60.
Increased explosive arrows per energize from 7 to 10.
Increased arrow stockpile from 50 to 70.
Increased explosive arrows per energize from 9 to 12.
[p align="start"]Charge Rifle
Increased max distance damage from 99 to 110.
Max damage occurs at >200m.
Decreased selectfire damage penalty from 40% to 25%.
[p align="start"]Dev Note: Mach 1 Gibby was really funny, but unintentional. Now, both he and Maggie should move as intended with their respective movement speed buffs and the Agile Standard Stock.
[p align="start"](Previously Hotfixed) Agile Standard Stock \

[p align="start"]Dev note: Heavy hitting shotguns can be inconsistent with their damage, either with chunky hits or lots of 11s. As such, it can be more difficult to unlock their respective hop-ups when compared to a full auto-weapon. Thus we are lowering the cost to unlock.

[p align="start"]Dev note: In this patch, we’re rolling out over 150 map-related Quality of Life fixes across the Outlands with a massive chunk of that polish going straight to World’s Edge. We’ve smoothed out sticky collisions to keep wall-bouncing and rotations fluid, patched up geo holes that were occasionally swallowing loot and Legends, and permanently closed off several unintended rat spots to maintain competitive integrity. Alongside these tweaks we’ve also cleaned up some clipping issues related to Alter’s Ultimate.

[p align="start"]Massive shoutout to our community for continuing to report these back to the team. Finding every hole, ledge or rat spot across the Outlands is a huge undertaking and the clips and bug reports you share are exactly what helps us track them down. Your feedback directly shapes the map health of Apex so keep sharing your clips.

[p align="start"]Welcome to the latest season of Apex Legends: MARKED. In addition to Bloodhound’s rework, buffs to Loba and Rampart, an energy weapon systems overhaul, and brand new Corrupted Attachments, we’re also bringing you a World’s Edge map rework, quality of life tweaks, and a slew of balancing changes. All of this is in pursuit of evolving Apex Legends into the best, most competitive Battle Royale out there. This season is going to push you and your squad to be the best you can possibly be, so get ready to group up, gear up, and dive into MARKED when it drops on August 4th, 2026!

[p align="start"]In Season 29, we ran two matchmaking tests — 1-Tier Premade Restrictions and Diamond+ Solo-Queue-Only — to experiment with variables to potentially use to address player frustrations in Ranked. Thank you to everyone who engaged with the tests and for the feedback you provided; it’s integral to helping us shape the future of the game mode. We are actively analyzing and evaluating the data from these tests, and are in the process of writing an upcoming blog to discuss the results and next steps. Keep an eye out for the followup comms in the coming weeks.

[p align="start"]We've beefed up our servers in Season 30. While not everyone will notice the difference, many players should experience increased stability, less lag, and lower chances of slo-mo servers across all game modes and regions. We're always working to improve the competitive experience for our players and, while these changes often take place behind the scenes, we’re excited to provide a noteworthy improvement for you all!

[p align="start"]Dev Note: We feel World’s Edge is in a solid place competitively, and have seen the sentiments echoed throughout the community, so our focus in updating the map was reducing disparity between POIs and delivering on players’ frequently requested changes, such as the return of Sorting Factory and Construction Stacks. To complement Bloodhound’s rework, we leveraged the new POIs in this update to move Bloodhound’s story forward in a meaningful way.
East Village
East Village: Added additional rock and tree cover in open areas around the POI

Sorting Factory: Added new platforms and ziplines around each train tunnel exit for smoother traversal

Stacks/Lava City: Placed additional platforms and buildings around the outskirts of the POI to improve rotations and endgames
Countdown: Improved quality of loot in the underground vault

Fixed a large amount of bugs, rat spots and navigational issues

[p align="start"]Dev note: Over the lifetime of Apex, Looting has changed substantially. A rising problem we wanted to address with these changes was the loot inflation and ease that players have around finding very high quality loot. In many cases, progressing through a match could feel like a quick spike at the beginning or mid point of the match and quite flat afterwards.

[p align="start"]We’ve overhauled several systems that were added over the past few years to shape a more engaging and straightforward loot chase for players. The spawn rates of high tier loot have been reduced across all maps, meaning that finding a rare Attachment will be a ‘rarer’ occurrence, and will signal a real shift in the power of your weapon.

[p align="start"]Arsenals provide a consistent way to get the guns you want, but can disrupt the game start by luring players into hot drop contests in the open spaces around Arsenals. Arsenals are now time locked, similar to EVO Harvesters. This ensures that they are available early game when you want them, but that your earliest fights off the drop are supplied only by what you can loot from the map. Unique loot sources such as Wildlife, Vaults, MRVNs, Ticks, and Rollers are still present but provide reduced quality of loot.
[p align="start"]TL;DR: Spawn rate of high tier loot has been reduced across all maps, which should shape a clearer and more cohesive looting experience.

[p align="start"]**For more information about the design approach and intention behind weapons systems and Legends changes, please read our recent Designer’s Notes.

[p align="start"]Dev note: We are updating how Weapon Stats are shown in game to improve transparency and readability of gameplay in Apex. You can now explore with greater detail than ever the unique stats and performance characteristics of each weapon. By exposing these stats and allowing players to examine how different attachments impact weapon performance, players can make more informed choices in-game quickly. Presenting this greater information with visual refinements is part of our effort to improve Onboarding and clarity of gameplay for all players.
New Playground tab available via Legend Locker > Weapons
Allows for you to preview information about the weapon, what attachments can go on the weapon, and how those attachments affect that weapon’s stats.
Changes here do not affect any in-game weapon behaviors.
[p align="start"]While looking at a weapon or attachment in the world or inventory:
The loot card now shows a detailed breakdown of a weapon’s damage, ideal range, rate of fire, firing modes and weapon specific gameplay information.
When looking at a weapon to swap, the loot card now shows a quick comparison between the weapon you are holding and the weapon you would pick up.
Can be disabled by changing Interact Prompt Style from Default to Compact.

[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/2YpT1TWUyyw4tid9iMOhZ6/165f6d01a7f1a379c301b4b02af201de/08..jpg?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.614453125,yPosition=0.4895833333333333" style="box-sizing: border-box; display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; object-fit: contain; height: 451.125px; width: 802px;"]
For attachments that can be equipped onto your weapon, the loot card now shows the stat change that will occur when equipped.
Can be disabled by changing Interact Prompt Style from Default to Compact.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Corrupted Attachments provide players with a meaningful choice when they are equipping their guns. Providing a unique blend of big buffs and negative stat trade offs will reshape a weapons performance and specialize its power. Limited to one Corrupted Attachment per weapon, players must make tactical decisions about their preferred loadouts. Need an absolute bullet hose for those close range fights? Put the Overflowing Mag on the R-99 for easier one-clips at the cost of longer reloads. Or do you want more maneuverability and speed? Put the Agile Standard Stock on the R-99 instead for increased movement speed at the cost of reduced mag size.
[p align="start"]New High Tier Attachment Rarity
Each Corrupted Attachment comes with a unique bonus and negative effect
Only 1 Corrupted Attachment can be equipped on a gun at a time
5 New Attachments
Overflowing Magazine
Improves magazine size beyond that of a Purple Magazine
Reduces weapon reload speed
Can be attached to any weapon that accepts a Magazine
Headseeker Barrel
Increases weapon Headshot Damage
Reduces Hipfire Accuracy
Improves recoil at the same level as the Purple Barrel

Improves Reload Speed

Improves Hipfire Accuracy at the same level as the Purple Laser Sight

Eliminates weapon move speed penalty

Improves Reload Speed and Weapon Handling at the same level as the Purple Standard Stock
Rapid Sniper Stock
Increases weapon Rate of Fire
Reduces Magazine Size
Improves Reload Speed and Weapon Handling at the same level as the Purple Sniper Stock

The core loot pool with a low spawn chance

[p align="start"]Dev note: We're taking a big swing with energy weapons this season and really shaking up their ammo systems. We've removed energy ammo entirely as a lootable item. The goal of this change was to provide another way to think about your weapon loadout choice, and why you are picking one weapon over another. To lean into their unique energy identity these weapons will now come with their own regenerating ammo pool. Removing the need to hunt for extra ammo or spend valuable inventory space opens up new loadout opportunities, but keep an eye on that stockpile - once it's run dry players will have to wait for it to regenerate. With replenishing ammo, we expect energy weapons to be most powerful in shorter fights, but start to lose ground in longer sustained engagements.
Energy Ammo boxes removed from the game
Energy Weapons come with a stockpile of ammunition
Similar to the Bocek or Care Package Weapons
Energy Weapon Stockpile Size is comprised of multiple magazines worth of ammo
Each weapon comes with
Havoc: 3 Magazines worth of stockpile
Nemesis: 3 Magazines worth of stockpile
Devotion: 3 Magazines worth of stockpile
L-Star: 4 Magazines worth of stockpile
RE-45: 2 Magazines worth of stockpile
Volt: 2 Magazines worth of stockpile
Triple Take: 2 Magazines worth of stockpile
If the weapons magazine size increases, the stockpile total updates to match
ex. A Volt with no extended magazine has a maximum Stockpile size of 40
ex. A Volt with a Purple Magazine has a maximum Stockpile size of 54
Energy Weapons regenerate a magazines worth of ammo over 18 seconds
Regeneration time does not increase if your magazine size increases
ex. A Volt with no extended magazine attachment equipped regenerates 20 shots over 18 seconds
ex. A Volt with a Purple Magazine equipped regenerates 27 shots over 18 seconds
Regeneration pauses while shooting or reloading the weapon
A new HUD element has been added for energy weapons. This displays how many magazines worth of ammo you have left.

[p align="start"]Dev note: Core to Apex is the Drop Ship experience, it is not only the game’s start, but it also influences a team's odds for success. A successful jump can be the difference between a top placement in a match and a quick trip back to the lobby. Timing and positioning your team for a good Drop is a skill check, and it is a responsibility that some players prefer to have in their direct control. Volunteering for Jumpaster empowers the more experienced and adventurous players who want to shape the start of their team’s game.

[p align="start"]In game modes with a Jumpmaster, during Character Select, players can now volunteer to be Jumpmaster. This adds a deterministic way for players to take on the responsibility of being the Jumpmaster for their team.
[p align="start"]During Character Select
When Volunteering is active, players will see an option to ‘Opt In To Jumpmaster’.
Players can press the corresponding button to Volunteer at any time during Character Selection.
Players who have Opted In to Jumpmaster will be marked on the UI in Character Select.
Players who volunteer for Jumpmaster on a match will be Opted In to Jumpmaster for future matches.
Players can use the same button press to Opt OUT of volunteering if they have previously Opted IN.
If more than one team member has Volunteered, Jumpmaster will be selected randomly from the group of Volunteers.
[p align="start"]The Marked Battle Pass Free Track features a meaningful weapon charm, Purrfect Pals, starring two adorable cats.

[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/5tLXIQss7BWPQlN52r0SzY/3670fb5bcc6ca24eb8c375c8492109dd/04..png?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.38011695906432746,yPosition=0.5896531452087007" style="box-sizing: border-box; display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; object-fit: contain; height: 451.125px; width: 802px;"]

[p align="start"]This charm was created to honour a former Respawn developer, Benjamin Sklar, who passed away last year, and was inspired by the things that were most meaningful to him, including his two beloved cats, Tia and Sophia. Our friend embodied a strong sense of social justice and fairness. He loved astronomy, travel and photography. His special interests included quantum physics and personal finances. We miss him dearly, but we are comforted knowing his legacy can live on in Apex Legends. Welcome to the Apex Games, Tia and Sophia.
[p align="start"]Back to top

[p align="start"]The Marked Seasonal Pack* brings Bloodhound-inspired divinity with a chance to unlock the “Allfather’s Fury” Mythic CAR. 5 customization tiers unlock through Exotic Shards, from base form through feather and wing evolutions, with Knock FX, Ordnance FX, and final rethemes.
[p align="start"]*Not available in all regions.
[p align="start"]Back to top

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Despite changes to Bloodhound’s kit in Season 28, they remain nearly invisible at middle-to-high tiers and have the lowest pick rate once you get to Gold tier and above. Luckily, we teased additional changes, and it’s finally time to show off Bloodhound’s refreshed kit. The biggest change is a brand new Ultimate, Allfather’s Cloak. This is a multifaceted cloaking tool that will help your squad ambush opponents or escape third-party situations. Combined with easier-to-use tracking tools from your Passive and Tactical, it’s much easier to gain an understanding of the battleground and then push in when enemies show weakness. The hope is that Bloodhound players feel like they can now play from the front foot, leading their squad and creating openings instead of just scanning some enemies and hoping your allies can take advantage.
[p align="start"]Passive
Bloodhound can now see a red trail near fresh enemy clues to guide you to them
This is similar to the red footsteps Bloodhound would see in their previous ultimate, Beast of the Hunt.
To reduce visual clutter, many types of clues have been removed. Traversal clues and Eliminations are the only ones that remain.
Trails and clues now get hidden when the owner dies, except the Player Killed clue
Adjusted some of the black raven behavior to help them spawn more reliably, and included information about how they work to the ability description
White ravens can fly up to 400m (was previously 190m baseline, 380m with Raven's Flight)
You can now activate white ravens remotely by looking at them for a short time
[p align="start"]Tactical
Tactical now full-body scans for 3 seconds (was a 2 second full-body scan with 2 more seconds of a diamond scan)
After the full-body scan finishes, create 4 "snapshot" scans with 1.5s in between them
If a scan hits a white raven and at least one enemy, cooldown no longer partially refunds
If a scan hits a white raven and no enemies, it still refunds the full cooldown
[p align="start"]Ultimate
New Ultimate: Allfather’s Cloak
Throw down a device that cloaks anyone who gets within range

[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/21AhTW7rsgFCNpxuYmGmun/7105c0b1dffc8fff5dc051f35c71a09b/06.__1_.jpg?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.6230398069963812,yPosition=0.37291280148423006" style="box-sizing: border-box; display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; object-fit: contain; height: 451.125px; width: 802px;"]
While cloaked, players also gain 20% increased movement speed and threat vision

[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/1rXjlCWDMZ9XqHGorzCzbN/55db5813b0cc9132949d3f5deefbb51f/07..png?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.31212121212121213,yPosition=0.5102389078498294" style="box-sizing: border-box; display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; object-fit: contain; height: 451.125px; width: 802px;"]
Cloaking area lasts 8 seconds
Cloak lasts 12 seconds after leaving the area
Cloak breaks when taking damage, firing your weapon, or when using most abilities
Bloodhound’s abilities can be used without breaking cloak
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Level 2
(NEW) Hidden Sight: Using the Ult refreshes your Tactical, and using your Tactical while cloaked hides the visuals effect from enemies
(NEW) Bird’s Eye: White ravens will split and fly to the two nearest enemies (on different squads)
Removed Taste of Blood, Raven's Flight buffed and integrated to base kit
Level 3
(NEW) True Predator: Shooting temporarily interrupts your cloak instead of breaking it

[p align="start"]Dev Note: While this season’s looting changes should improve Loba’s value as she improves her team’s loot quality, we felt like she could use some buffs to help improve her ability to stay alive and support the team. Her tactical deploys much faster, and her ultimate cooldown is being reduced to make sure she can continually deliver the goods to her squadmates.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Reduced time taken to equip (was 0.6s, now 0.4s)
Projectile range has been increased by roughly 15% and projectile travel time has been reduced by roughly 30%
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Cooldown reduced to 120s (was 150s)
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Level 3 Upgrade Brand New Bag now grants purple bags instead of gold bags (since gold bags will no longer spawn)

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Despite significant buffs, Rampart still has trouble competing in the current meta. She can be extremely strong if she gets bunkered up in a good position, but it is otherwise difficult to make work. Her Passive can be underwhelming depending on the strength of LMGs, so we’re adding a new layer. We’re also improving her mobility with Sheila to help her in fights against more mobile opposition.
[p align="start"]Passive
In addition to the other benefits, she now gains locked hop-up progress 50% faster
[p align="start"]Tactical
Wall health increased at lower EVO levels (was 400/600/800, now 600/700/800)
Amped wall health increased by 25
Wall deployment time reduced by 0.5s
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Increased base move speed while firing or spinning Sheila (was 70, now 104)
This matches the previous movement speed with the Ramped Up Upgrade. Ramped Up still upgrades base move speed by the same amount as before (takes you from 104 to 139)
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Level 2 Upgrade Combat Reserve no longer grants red weapon access (since those are going away). It now grants stowed reloads in addition to its other benefits.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Valk has remained in the upper tier in terms of pick rates for several seasons now. As we continually try to level the playing field, it feels like time to reduce Valk’s power level. There are two main goals - reduce her “artillery” power, which rivals other characters who don’t have jetpacks, as well as make her Ultimate a bit easier to counter.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Base damage reduced from 25 to 15 (each additional rocket still does 3 damage)
Adjust the missile’s attack angle as they approach their target
This reverts an element of her Season 27 changes, where the missiles were able to fly over tall walls or buildings and dive straight down on top of players
[p align="start"]Ultimate
15% Ult base height reduction (reverts the Afterburners Upgrade that was moved baseline in 27.0)
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Level 2 Upgrade Eye In the Sky: Reduced through-walls scan distance to 100m (no change if you have line of sight - keeps the full 250m range)
Level 3 Upgrade Supersonic: Reduction in the blast-off time improvement (now reduces launch time by 40% instead of 50%)

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Axle’s pick rate has been trending in a healthier direction with each subsequent nerf, however, we understand her Kickstart drone is still too oppressive in too many contexts. On Axle’s release, players had the option to access double Tac or double Ult charges. Nitro Gates and Kickstart Drones have been everywhere, and it’s given everyone plenty of opportunities to learn how to use (and how to react) to her kit. Her Tac can help her entire team quickly close a gap. Her Ult can launch victims into the air. The strength of those outputs is not lost on us, and some of the changes over the season have simply been to limit the availability of some strong abilities. Other changes have been attempts to expand counterplay opportunities or change the context of when her abilities are strongest. The nerfs in this season are in the vein of the latter; we’ll see how Axle-related fights are affected and, if she’s still a menace to deal with in too many situations, we’ll take an even more heavy handed approach.
[p align="start"]Tactical
Reduced max slide boost time from 5 seconds to 3 seconds
[p align="start"]Ultimate
Now affects self & allies (similar to Mad Maggie, Bangalore, and Gibraltar ultimates)
Axle (self) gets damaged, stunned, and displaced (same as enemies)
Allies get stunned and displaced, but won’t take damage
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Replace Automata with Long Haul, which brings the Tac max slide time back up to 5 seconds
Shuffled order
Lvl 2: Sliding Shooter vs Long Haul
Lvl 3: Jump Gate vs Super Slider

[p align="start"]Dev note: We have seen the frustrations surrounding Seer – his Tactical can feel oppressive, and is being encountered at an increased rate – and are continuing to address them. The changes we’ve made so far have been meant to reduce the frequency with which you'll encounter Seer's Tactical. At split start, the most picked Upgrades (2 Tac charges / reduced Tac cooldown in Ult) saw ~90% and ~80% pick rates, respectively. When combined, players have access to 2 Tac charges on a very short cooldown. By moving both to level 3, players can only have one. These changes have helped address complaints of Tactical spamming in Ult, while keeping the intended power of those two Upgrades in place. As we discussed in our most recent Designer's Notes, Seer is a tricky Legend to balance, as a prominent Seer meta is an oppressive one. We will also reduce the amount of turn slow so you shouldn’t feel like you’re stun locked.
[p align="start"]Upgrades
Reduced the Home Base (Faster Tact Charge in Ult zone) Upgrade modifier to 2.5. This will make the Tactical cooldown 8 seconds instead of 5 while in the Ult zone.
Moved Home Base Upgrade to level 3
Moved Energizing Focus (Regen shield on tact hit) Upgrade to level 2
[p align="start"]Tactical
Reduced the amount of turn slow that was being applied
[p align="start"]Back to top

[p align="start"]Dev Note: We want the Hemlok to remain a stable mid-range assault rifle, but its ability to counter Legend utility has heavily contributed to its dominance in the meta. Pulling back on the power of the Breach Charge keeps it viable while making space for other ARs.
[p align="start"]Hemlok Breach AR

Reduced damage done to Hardlight and structures by 50%
Reduced damage to 21 (was 22)

[p align="start"]Dev Note: The Alternator, RE-45, and R-99 are receiving reductions in damage and magazine size. These guns are currently significantly outperforming other short range options. These adjustments ensure they remain fast damage dealers while requiring more precision to secure knocks.
[p align="start"]Alternator SMG

Reduced damage in Double Tap to 14 per bullet (was 15)
Magazine Size

Accelerator Hop-Up equipped on all gold weapons without an existing Hop-Up
[p align="start"]Accelerator
Gain 15% ultimate charge on knock with the weapon
Includes a 3 second assist window

No longer gives ultimate charge from damage done with the weapon

Increased points to unlock on the Devotion to 500 (was 425)

Hi all, just pushed a couple more fixes.
Octane's jump pads will no longer bounce unintended objects (thank you for making the most of this bug with firing range clips, they made us chuckle).

After resolving issues causing error code:truck on Steam and EA App last week, we're happy to confirm that this error code has been fixed on all consoles as well. Thank you for your patience on this issue.
Seer

Dev note: We have seen the frustrations surrounding Seer and are making urgent changes. The above changes are meant to reduce the frequency with which you'll encounter Seer's Tactical. At split start, the the most picked Upgrades (2 Tac charges / reduced Tac cooldown in Ult) saw ~90% and ~80% pick rates, respectively. When combined, players have access to 2 Tac charges on a very short cooldown. By moving both to level 3, players can only have one. These changes should address complaints of Tactical spamming in Ult, while keeping the intended power of those two upgrades in place. As we discussed in our most recent Designer's Notes, Seer is a tricky Legend to balance, as a prominent Seer meta is an oppressive one; we will continue to monitor Seer's performance and make additional adjustments as necessary.

Recently we mentioned that changes to Bot Royale Evolved would ensure only one player squad in each match. This was a miscommunication, as most* matches will only have one squad. In it's current state, we're seeing 2 teams in ~5% of matches, closer to 15% in peak hours. We'll continue to monitor match data and sentiment toward the game mode.
We have now resolved the connection issues that were preventing players from connecting to the game. Thanks for your patience while we worked on a fix.
We're aware that some players are having trouble connecting to our servers. We're working on a fix and will share an update as soon as we have more information.
Hey all, we just made a couple adjustments to our game modes based on community feedback.

In response to community feedback, we are converting Wildcard map rotations to a 90 minute timer! We are making this change to align with community desires and may test variations in rotation timing in future, all in pursuit of finding what players enjoy most.
We have reduced Bot Royale Evolved lobbies to contain only one player squad with broad teammate matchmaking bands.

Since Bot Royale evolved we've seen frustration around two prominent pain points: long queue times, and wide skill disparity between squads - both stemming from the 1-5 team lobby parameter. This change should allow players to get into matches much quicker and with less frustration towards your opponents. releases.displayName: Apex Legends™: Overclocked Midseason Patch Notes

items.text: [p align="start"]Welcome back to Overclocked Split 2! To start the latter half of the season, we’re bringing Legend balancing changes, new shotgun hop-ups, and various fixes and improvements that we think you’re going to like a lot. With all these changes landing on June 23rd, it’s the perfect time to grab your squad and dive into Overclocked!

[p align="start"]We cannot overstate the value we put on competitive integrity in Apex Legends; hopefully you’ve seen our incremental and seasonal recap account ban updates. We have also been working hard behind the scenes to eradicate less conventional hacks. This season, we implemented detection for a reverse speed hack, preventing cheaters from freezing themselves mid-air for long stretches of time. Additionally, we identified and resolved numerous exploits that could be used to take down servers. Combatting cheaters is a constant cat and mouse game, as such, we are not always able to discuss all the things we’re working on, lest we tip our hand to bad actors. Rest assured, we are committed to making Apex Legends the cleanest it can possibly be, and we are working on things that we’re excited to be able to share with you soon. Please continue to report suspected cheaters, your reports help inform our anti-cheat work!
BALLISTIC

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Ballistic has been strong in the past but after a bunch of nerfs he’s fallen close to the bottom in pickrate. We wanted to bring some of his power back but we understand he was pretty frustrating to fight against in his prime. This goal with his Tactical buff is to bring back some of the previous numbers but we wanted to add more counterplay options for the victims. The speed boost on the Ultimate was also very powerful but it could make Ballistic’s team very difficult to fight. Instead, we’re only giving a sprint boost which should still allow for fast pushes as a team but not a speed advantage during the fight.
Passive
Ballistic now respawns with his Sling weapon in all game modes.
Tactical
Overheat now only applies to one weapon.
If a player has a weapon out when hit by Whistler the overheat debuff applies only to that weapon.
If the player is unarmed when hit by Whistler it applies to the weapon in the first weapon slot.
Overheat no longer degrades when not firing or swapping to another weapon.
Overheat does not increment when swapping to another weapon and shooting.
Overheat damage increased from 15 to 50.
Overheat debuff duration increased from 12 to 15.
Tactical charges increased from 1 to 2.
Decreased time between firing and when homing activates.
The overheat debuff no longer re-applies if you hit someone who is already overheating and you cannot apply it to multiple guns on the same player.
Ultimate
Ballistic and teammates within range get a sprint boost when his Ultimate is activated. (Previously only Ballistic got a speed boost)
Sprint boost will only apply a speed boost while sprinting and will not speed up other types of movement.
Upgrades
Level 2
Extra Bullet: Gain an additional Tactical charge.
Trap Mode: When placed in the world, Ballistic’s KTactical lasts 15 seconds and deals 35 damage if an enemy walks into it.
Level 3
Quiet Time: Ballistic’s Tactical no longer applies overheat. Instead it adds silence and slow on hit. It also has a longer cooldown.
Killing Time: Now moved to level 3, still provides a 15 second extension to Ballistic’s Ultimate.
PATHFINDER

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Your favourite friendly robot has been a bit outclassed by other skirmishers. We wanted to touch the uptime on his abilities to help him keep pace and improve his Upgrades to be more in line with other Legends that get perks from other classes.
Passive
Pathfinder now tucks in his legs while riding horizontal ziplines.
This should make him a little harder to hit when riding on his Ultimate and other ziplines in the world.
Tactical
Tactical charges increased from 1 to 2.
Removed the progressive cooldown and it is now a flat 20 seconds.
Ultimate
Increased launch speed of the zipline projectile.
Reduced cooldown from 3 minutes to 2 minutes.
Upgrades
Level 2
Field Research: Now grants all Recon perks instead of just the survey beacon scan.
Ringmaster: Now grants all Controller perks instead of just the ring console access.
Level 3
Landing Gear: Grants more air control and faster recovery from hard landings. This replaces the 2 Tactical charges Upgrade.
SEER

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Seer saw a bit of an uptick after his last set of buffs but has settled back down toward the bottom. He is, however, seeing some play in higher Ranked lobbies so we know he has potential. For this update we focused on quality of life buffs. We’ve done a pass on making his Passive and Tactical more responsive.
Passive
Increased the activation speed of the heartbeat sensor.
Decreased the interval time between heartbeats.
Decreased activation time for unarmed ADSing
Made the delay when aiming more consistent between weapon and unarmed.
This means the heartbeat sensor will appear at the same time regardless of the weapon you’re using.
Tactical
Reduced the delay between the launch and hit.
Improved the slow on hit, should now halt faster moving Legends more effectively.
Ultimate
Upon deployment, there is now a quick 2 second scan of the area which will highlight any enemy in the area.
Enemies that enter the area after it’s deployed will also be scanned for 2 seconds.
Cloaked enemies will now show footsteps if they are within the Ultimate zone.
AXLE

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Axle has undeniably pushed the pace of play. With these nerfs, we want to target areas that cause the most frustration while staying true to her identity as an aggressive lateral speedster with team utility. Considering the popularity of her “Super Slider” upgrade, her Tactical has simply been available too frequently, nullifying much of the risk that should be considered when overextending. We also saw an opportunity to add some agency to Kickstart victims, when evading or destroying the drone simply isn’t an option.
Tactical
Reduced max in-world count from 3 to 2.
Reduced hp from 150 to 100.
Passive/Tactical

Knocked players can no longer slide across zip codes as Axle or while under the effect of a Nitro Gate. They can still boost through a Nitro Gate, but once the effect times out, they will slow down accordingly.
Upgrades
"Super Slider" Upgrade no longer grants a second Tactical charge. Instead, it now grants Nitro Gate a 5 second cooldown reduction and +1 max in-world count.
Ultimate
Kickstart now displaces victims on a parabolic arc based on their velocity at the moment of impact, instead of straight up.
Reduced enemy highlight duration slightly to better match stun duration.
MAD MAGGIE

[p align="start"]Dev note: Maggie has been a top performer for a while and, with the rise of Gibby, she’s seeing even more play. She is doing a lot and her Tactical is completely controlling the battlefield. Her Ultimate creates an issue similar to previous-era-Ballistic, where the added speed boost is making players very difficult to lock down. In this case, we’re introducing a series of nerfs to bring her pick rate down to a more healthy space.
Tactical
Increased Cooldown from 22 seconds to 28 seconds.
Ultimate
The speed boost granted from running on the pucks dropped by the wrecking ball has been replaced by a sprint boost.
Will no longer speed up all movement, just when sprinting.
VALKYRIE

[p align="start"]Dev note: Valkyrie is becoming one of the top picked Legends and has been performing really well over the last few seasons. We are making a minor adjustment to help assuage frustrations and manage her climbing pickrate. We understand this doesn’t address other aspects of her kit that are strong, but we are continuing to monitor her match data and will make additional changes if necessary.
Passive
Removed the recent improvement, which allowed her to land faster from skydiving.
CONDUIT

[p align="start"]Dev note: Since her changes at the beginning of Season 29, Conduit spiked to the top of the pick rates and remained at that spot several weeks later. We’re so excited to see that players have really felt the improvements to Conduit’s supportive agency and playmaking potential. However, we recognize that she has been a key enabler of Legends that push the meta in an extremely aggressive way. Additionally, her dominance crowds out all other Support Legends, making her an obvious pick. Finally, she was present in 8 of the top 10 most popular team compositions. All of these indicators point to an unhealthy balance state and, as a result, we want to take steps to slow things down a bit.
Tactical
Decreased Regen Rate from 15/s to 10/s
Increased Regen Duration from 6s to 8s
Decreased Ally Total Regen from 90 to 80
Decreased Conduit Total Regen from 60 to 56
Upgrades
Level 3
Instant Barrier: Increased Regen Duration from 4s to 6s
Tactical
Increased Cooldown from 27 seconds to 30 seconds
Upgrades
Level 3
Enduring Barrier: No longer grants regen through ring damage

[p align="start"]Dev Note: The Hemlok Breach AR has stayed pretty dominant in the meta since its release, even through a few rounds of adjustments. Its damage per magazine has always been pretty generous, so the following change aims to tone down the dominance at higher tiers.
Hemlok Breach AR
White magazine reduced from 21 to 20
Blue magazine reduced from 24 to 22
Purple and gold magazines reduced from 27 to 25
EVA-8
Small increase to handling speed.
Mozambique
Small increase to handling speed.
[p align="start"]Dev Note: We’re introducing a new hop-up and juggling around another, for all the information about why check out our latest edition of Designer’s Notes.
Executioner \
Available on: Peacekeeper and Mastiff
Knocking an enemy with the weapon grants 50 shield regeneration over 10 seconds
375 points to unlock
Dual Shell
Removed from: Mastiff
Disruptor Rounds
Removed from: Peacekeeper
Graffiti Mod
Removed from: Longbow DMR, Wingman and Mozambique
Added to: Flatline and Volt

[p align="start"]Dev Note: It’s been a while since Nemesis has seen some updates from us, so it’s time… Turbo Nemi has arrived. The weapon will become fully heated after two bursts, allowing it to fire at its maximum fire rate much quicker.
Turbocharger
Added to: Nemesis \[600 points to unlock]

items.text: As of 3:20pm PT: We have pushed a fix to today's matchmaking issues. Players should now be able to access matches without issue. Thank you, again, for your patience.

As of 11:20pm PT: Our fix to resolve the matchmaking outage resulted in an adjacent, unforeseen issue now preventing players from joining matches. Our team is continuing to work on this and is hoping to have it resolved ASAP.
As of 10:49am PT: We have resolved the issues that were preventing players from joining a match. Players should now be able to enter matchmaking as intended. Thank you for your ongoing patience.
We are aware players are currently unable to connect to a match. We are aware and are investigating. Thank you for your patience.
Hi all, after a brief delay, we have started the following matchmaking test:
[p align="start"]Players can only join premade squads containing squadmates with a differential of ONE Ranked tier (down from two).

[p align="start"]As a reminder, we are looking to create tighter lobbies; our expectation is that, by limiting players from creating squads with wide skill bands, you will more consistently match against similar-skilled opponents, creating a more fair, competitive experience.
[p align="start"]The test will run until the end of the split (June 23rd).
Improved transition screen UI to better indicate the game is still loading
Reduced the color overlay effect of Conduit's passive
We resolved an issue where players were able to exploit Axle's movement, resulting in an indefinite slide

We are temporarily disabling voice comms for players on Xbox systems to investigate their contribution to a game crash. Xbox players will not be able to hear or speak to other players, regardless of platform.
We are also investigating a recent issue resulting in FPS drops, likely tied to specific CPUs.: We will provide updates as they become available to us!

We are looking into an issue preventing players from purchasing the Ultimate+ Battle Pass tier on any Xbox platform. Our current recommended workaround is to try from the Microsoft Store, where possible.
We are also tracking a crash impacting Xbox Series machines. We have located the issue and are working towards a fix.
We're hoping to have these issues resolved soon and will relay updates as they come.

Overclocked is locked and loaded and ready to go! In Season 29 of the Apex Games we are not only focused on delivering exciting, new seasonal content, but addressing key feedback from our player-base. A brand new Legend, Axle, joins the fray and this combat racer is bound to shake things up. Vantage, Conduit and Ash are getting buffs to keep up with the breakneck pace. We’re introducing Deathbox Respawns and Chained Healing to get you and your teammates back into the fight sooner. The starting line approaches, so get ready to roll in Apex Legends: OVERCLOCKED.

To get a quick overview of some of Overclocked’s main updates, check out our Highlights blog from last week. For a deep-dive into meta balancing, check out our seasonal Designer’s Notes. Read on for all the details about what’s happening this season!
Solo-Queueing Adjustments

We’ve heard the continued feedback on solo queueing difficulty. Later this split, we’ll introduce a system where solo players matchmake against opponents of a slightly lower skill tier in both Ranked and Unranked matches. This is aimed at reducing the advantage of full premade squads and tightening win rate gaps between solos and three-stacks.
Queue Time Tuning in High-Skill Lobbies

Late in 28.1, we began rolling out longer max queue times for higher-skill players. We’re keeping these changes in place to help create tighter skill bands and reduce mismatched games (e.g. Plats vs. Masters), leading to more competitive matches overall.
The majority of players will see no difference at all. If you matchmake into smaller pools, for example during off-hours, then you may have to wait up to a few minutes longer than before
Bots in Unranked Modes

We’re continuing limited testing of bots in select regions and skill ranges in Unranked modes (Trios, Duos, Wildcard). The goal is to improve match quality by reducing extreme skill mismatches and avoiding excessively long queue times, particularly if there are lower-population scenarios. Bots are used only to fill gaps in these scenarios, not replace full matches, and you will never matchmake with an Apex Bot on your team.
This season, as a quality of life update, we have improved voice chat clarity and added the ability to adjust voice chat volumes for each member of your squad individually.

We are continuing our work to resolve existing audio issues and improve in-match audio quality so that you can consistently rely on these systems to inform your situational awareness. We are aware that audio issues increased during the recent Gundam Event and we are continuing to work on methods to avoid similar situations in the future. We pushed various stability improvements over the latter half of Season 28 that have improved the situation, pushing us towards cleaner audio experiences. We appreciate the reports we received - they greatly helped our ongoing investigations.

Dev note: With this new mechanic, we wanted to introduce an alternative way to get your teammates back into the fight, faster (but riskier) than the classic Respawn Beacon process, that feels like a reward for teams that successfully clear and hold an area. The safest option will remain disengaging, recovering banners, moving to a safe beacon, and respawning. But a successful Deathbox Respawn may bring your team back to full strength before a third party can capitalize on your weakened squad.
Respawn dead teammates directly from their Deathbox.
High Risk: Respawning at a Deathbox is loud, visible to nearby enemies, and takes 7 seconds. Be sure to clear the area before attempting it.
Respawn with Your Gear: When respawned from your Deathbox, any weapons and gear that still remain unlooted are added to your inventory automatically.
Lockout Timer: Each additional death increases the time before teammates can use Deathbox Respawn again. Stay alive to reset the timer.

Dev note: Respawn from Dropship is a dangerous and lengthy process. Often the surviving player activating the Respawn Beacon will get pounced on and killed before their teammates disembark the Respawn Dropship. This change is meant to get boots on the ground faster for returning players, while keeping the Dropship visible for the entire lobby for an extended duration, ensuring no enemies miss the cue that players are returning to the battlefield.
Animation timing adjusted
Dropship arrival shortened so respawned players re-enter the game faster.
Dropship hover time after respawn increased.

Dev note: This is a Quality of Life change at its core. Many factors contribute to when and how you heal. Limited resources and timing influence this choice: often meaning that you’re going to spam heal several shield cells rather than wasting the more valuable and limited shield batteries you have. This change is meant to make that existing pattern of spamming the heal button to rip 4 cells in a row smoother and less repetitive.
While healing, another healing item may now be queued to automatically begin once the current healing action finishes.
There are 3 settings options (‘Single’ is the new default option) that can be changed via the Gameplay settings menu:
Off: Disables the feature and leaves the current healing system unaffected.
Single: While healing, allows the queuing of another healing item. You must queue each additional heal manually by pressing the heal button again, or selecting a new item from the healing wheel.

Auto: While healing, allows the queuing of another healing item. Auto will continuously queue that same healing item, without any further input, until the effective health pool is full, or you run out of that healing item.

We have overhauled the Health Bar system to increase reliability and improve Line of Sight checks when obscuring effects are present. Effects such as smoke and foliage will now more consistently block the LoS check used for Health Bars. This means Health Bars will appear less often in situations where an enemy is obscured to you.

Dev note: Axle was born after a big-picture assessment of the state of movement in Apex following Valkyrie’s two-year reign in the ALGS. Valk was a big pick in competitive play, and on the other side of the competitive spectrum, Octane was the perennial #1 pick. Other Legends with movement abilities have consistently been mainstays in the top five.

This comes as no surprise; fluid movement has always been a staple of Apex, a powerful tool in a BR where positioning is paramount. Our movement deep-dive preceding Axle’s development shone a light on our biggest learning: Characterizing “Movement” as a tool is far too reductive. Just look online: community-driven movement wikis and training videos are everywhere. Movement is the toolbox, and every jetpack boost, soft landing, and grapple is just one of many tools inside.
Keep your head on a swivel, because Axle transforms the battlefield into her racetrack.
Class
Skirmisher
Passive
DRIFT: Increased control while sliding.
Axle accelerates and moves faster than others while sliding.
She also has increased lateral control.
Tactical
NITRO GATE: Deploy a speed gate that sends users into a boosted slide.
Stepping into a Nitro Gate forces users into a speedy slide, where they have greatly increased velocity and lateral control.
This effect lasts for up to five seconds as long as speed isn’t naturally slowed.
Manually stopping the slide will end the effect (although it can be maintained through quick b-hops).
The gate is team agnostic, meaning it has the same effect on friendlies and enemies, though Axle will be the only one with increased slide control.
Ultimate
KICKSTART: Deploy an enemy-seeking drone that displaces targets on impact.
Axle fires a drone straight out in front of her, where it traverses close to the ground in a straight line as it scans for enemies in a wide FoV.
Once an enemy is spotted, the drone seeks towards the target, closing the gap to get within detonation range.
If the target cannot outrun or destroy the drone before detonation, it will knockback all targets in range up into the air.
Victims are revealed while airborne, take explosive damage, and are briefly stunned.
Upgrades
Level 2
Super Slider: Gain a second Tactical charge.
Automata: Gain a second Ultimate charge.
Level 3
Jump Gate: Upgrades the Nitro Gate to give a double-jump.
Similar to how Octane’s Triple Jump upgrade works, this upgrades the Nitro Gate itself.
Players can use up to one double-jump while the Nitro Gate effect is active.
Sliding Shooter: Bullets shot while sliding come straight from inventory instead of magazine.
Functionally, this allows for longer continuous firing while sliding before having to reload.

Bullets shot straight from inventory are capped at half the weapon’s max magazine size (i.e. if a purple mag capacity is 30 bullets, 15 bullets will get pulled from inventory before instantly transitioning to the active clip).

Dev note: Vantage is currently underperforming in fights and as a result is seeing less play overall. Looking over her kit we recognized that, as a sniper, her role becomes more and more difficult the later the game goes on (and playspace shrinks). We really wanted to find ways to keep her kit powerful at every stage of the game.
Passive
Tracking a team with Spotters Lens will generate 70% of an ultimate bullet
10 second cooldown per team
Tactical
Vantage is immune to hard landings exiting the tac
Increased velocity from 20 Meters Per Second to 21 Meters Per Second
Increased double jump range from 4m to 7m
Reduced deceleration at final destination by ~25%
Cooldown reduced from 20s to 17s
Ultimate
Toggle fire to equip your Canted Sight: A 2x optic mounted on the side of the rifle
While canted rechamber time is decreased from 1.2s to 1.1s
While canted ADS time reduced from 0.5s to 0.4s
Bullet scaling is drastically reduced in Canted sights (so be accurate!)
Increase aiming responsiveness with Normal sight
Reduced ADS time from 0.6s to 0.5s
Increased weapon handling in both modes
Reduced Holster and Lower time from 0.5s to 0.4s
Reduced Deploy and Raise time from 1.5s to 1.3s
Default Normal scope magnification increased from 3x to 4x
Upgrades
Tactical Cooldown replaced with Herd Tracker: Pinging an enemy will track the entire team

Dev note: As a Legend with a low pick rate that performs quite well relative to other Support Legends, Conduit presents an intriguing design conundrum: why aren’t more players picking her if her match result stats are great? Our primary goals are to keep Conduit feeling challenging but rewarding, to increase her playmaking potential, and also to provide her with more opportunities to have successful supportive interactions with her team.
Abilities
New Effect: If Savior’s Speed is active when sprinting toward a Skirmisher, gain an additional 5% movement speed.

Dev note: This season we're taking a big look at macro rotations and the options our maps provide alongside the tools our Legends bring to the table.

In previous updates we've implemented changes and adjustments to the Tridents to try and provide interesting and exciting gameplay opportunities. They're however not hitting the mark on what we want out of vehicle gameplay in Apex so we're removing them to let our Legends take the wheel. We've seen players consistently use Tridents in ways that wander far from their intended use: rotating between POIs. We feel we can better achieve this goal of speedy rotations with the existing state of Legend movement, putting another layer of importance on your team comp choices.

The Ziprails in Broken Moon have always helped define the overall feel of the map and how teams rotate between POIs. However those Ziprails also contribute to a lot of silent third parties that can feel particularly frustrating. We've gone through and removed the majority of rotational POI-to-POI Ziprails while maintaining the Ziprails within POIs that help define the combat space. This should make navigating the map feel a little more predictable and easier to understand.

We want squad compositions and Legend choices to really matter when it comes to how teams traverse through our maps. Pulling back on how quickly players can rotate via Legend-agnostic map tools puts that power back in our Legends hands.

We know our community experienced some server issues last week. Thank you to everyone who took the time to send in reports to us. To show our appreciation for your continued patience, everyone has been granted 1 Epic Apex Pack (please login within 2 weeks to claim it).
We wanted to share a quick recap of the recent server outages and what we have learned from them.

Two separate instances caused our servers to go down last week. One was due to rotating out Storm Point (due to persistent crashes for specific devices on that map) and replacing it with E-District. The initial swap ran into some issues, and then later on, as servers continued to try to incorrectly search for games on Storm Point, it caused players to no longer be able to get into games. We’ve now implemented a new internal process to avoid this mismatch in the future.

The other cause of servers going down was due to a prior fix for some performance monitoring systems that incorrectly handled how invalid data was processed. The fix was rolled back, which solved the issues, and we’ll be targeting another fix further down the road.
Ensuring the best possible experience in Apex Legends is a priority for us. We will continue to keep you updated as we continue our investigations and make further improvements.

We are temporarily removing Storm Point from map rotation on all modes and will be replacing it with E-District (daytime) while we continue to chase a permanent fix for a crash occurring on specific devices when Storm Point is active. We will provide more updates on this matter once we have them.

In addition, April Fools LTM is now reactivated today until Mon the 6th at 12pm PT for those that missed their first chance to play. Charged Up Wildcard Modes will still be available to play. Make sure to tune in for all the fun!
Thank you for your patience while we made this change! If you had any difficulty getting into a match, you should be able to now.

[p align="start"]Getting rushed? Unleash the power of the EMP Blast to stun enemies and damage placeable objects. Then recharge your EMP Battery by blocking damage with the Vortex Shield, collecting EVO, or with new Wild Cards.

Bigger and Better: Greatly increases the size of the Vortex Shield, speeds up deploy and stow time
Duck and Cover: Increases the Vortex Shield’s protective area but disables return fire
Energy Efficient: EMP Blast costs 50% energy (two uses per charge)
Sonic Boom: Upgrades the EMP Blast damage and adds knockback
Static Charge: EMP Battery remains fully charged even when used
Extra Juice: Revives grant EMP Battery charge
Background Process: Adds passive EMP Battery charging that increases while sprinting
Kinetic Converter: Increases movement speed based on EMP Battery charge percentage
Heat Signature: Spend EMP Battery charge to highlight enemies through walls

[p align="start"]We are making a couple adjustments to in-match audio to align with our continued commitment to provide the most informative audio experience possible.

Vault Keys

[p align="start"]Dev Notes: Vault Keys can be an important piece of loot, but getting baited by a red box with the hopes of a Kraber to be dashed by a Vault Key can feel terrible. This change will retain their rarity but no longer let them drive a deathboxes rarity tier.
[p align="start"]New In-Combat Healing System
Apex Bots will attempt to find cover and heal when damaged during combat Use these moments to push!
[p align="start"]New Target Acquisition and Awareness System
Apex Bots will make more intelligent decisions around which target to focus on. They'll be harder to sneak up on.

Apex Bots will switch weapons based on the distance from the target. Get too close, and if Apex Bots have a shotgun - watch out!

Apex Bots will utilize the various movement mechanics around the map like ziplines, ziprails, jump towers and more, to traverse and pursue.
Fixed the audio mix setting not saving properly on consoles
Lowered volume of Hardlight mesh breaking, as per community feedback
Increased volume of footsteps from enemies outside your field of view
Volume further increases as the source of the footsteps gets further behind you (ie. loud when beside you, louder when over your shoulder, loudest when directly behind you)
PC: Apex now uses the Windows Audio Session API (WASAPI) for microphone input.
This enables support in Windows 11 for the "Voice Clarity" audio enhancement, which you can enable to help remove unwanted background audio.
The option can be found in Window settings. Go to "System > Sound > Mic Properties" and look for "Audio Enhancements" in "Input settings".
Note: if you have multiple microphones connected to your PC & the game is using the wrong one you can either...
Select a specific microphone in Apex's Audio settings in the Voice Chat settings, see "Voice Chat Input Device" option.
Or set your mic "as default for communications" in Windows settings and then use the System Default option in Apex's Voice Chat settings.
Static objects now use bindless resources and batching to significantly reduce draw calls, improving baseline CPU performance for map rendering
Olympus uses improved algorithms to generate occlusion culling data structures, slightly improving CPU performance on the map.

PC: Uses ReBAR for faster uploads of data to the GPU, on systems that support it. This can reduce pop-in of models and textures and also use less time on the CPU, which can help performance stability.
More accurate reflection intensity in dark areas
Improvements to the clarity of ambient occlusion and specular occlusion
